findings.summary: The assertion-property fix landed in the ADR but NOT in the backlog-notes copy, and the two now say opposite things about the same three fixtures. ADR-0036:119-125 (staged) says: 'WHAT THEY MUST ASSERT, not what data they must carry: the PER-SEGMENT triple, after round-trip and after commitAll, on a fixture whose triple varies in at least one field per segment. Two earlier drafts prescribed fixture DATA and were wrong in both directions. The mutation none of the three catches today is the PARTIAL hoist -- podId per segment, incarnation and flushSeq per delta -- because BatchingSequencerTest asserts only hasSize(2).' backlog-notes.md:259-263 still carries the retracted fixture-DATA form verbatim: 'BatchedCommitDeltaTest round-trips a three-segment three-pod delta, golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin carries two distinct segments, and BatchingSequencerTest asserts a two-pod commitAll. Give those fixtures differing incarnationId or flushSeq PER SEGMENT ... and it dies at T0.' Two measured defects in that sentence. (a) It is false for the third fixture: BatchingSequencerTest.java:259-261 asserts `assertThat(delta.segments()).as("both submissions are in the entry").hasSize(2)` and nothing else about the segments, so varying the request data changes no assertion outcome and the partial hoist survives -- which is precisely what the ADR measured and what the notes deny by saying 'it dies at T0'. (b) golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin is named as one of 'those fixtures' to be given differing per-segment data, i.e. regenerated -- while ADR-0036:132-134 in the same commit says the opposite ('Existing goldens are untouched, so the DISCRIMINATING golden is a NEW file beside chain-delta-batched-v1.bin rather than an edit to it'), and GoldenChainEntryTest's own javadoc (format/src/test/java/binjava/format/GoldenChainEntryTest.java:21-28) says 'Do NOT regenerate these to make the test pass ... either the format changed again -- non-negotiable 8 applies, another version and another golden file -- or a reader broke.' The M4.10 baselines entry staged in this same commit names this exact class -- 'fixing one copy of a fact and missing its duplicates' -- and the notes are the copy an M4.10c session reads first, since backlog.md's M4.10c row links to it and not to the ADR body.
findings.failure_scenario: An M4.10c session follows backlog-notes.md#m410c. Path (a): it gives BatchedCommitDeltaTest and BatchingSequencerTest per-segment-varying incarnations, adds no new assertion beyond hasSize(2), sees green, and lands an encoder or a BatchingSequencer merge that writes podId per segment but hoists incarnationId and flushSeq once per delta. Every M4 production delta is single-segment, so the tree stays green through M4 and M5's first forwarded multi-pod batch drops every pod but one -- the exact shape the ADR flags as its M5-invisible failure, shipped with a full test suite passing. Path (b): it edits golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin to carry the new per-segment fields, GoldenChainEntryTest goes green against the new encoder, and the tree loses its only proof that a v1-kinded batched delta written by an earlier build still parses -- every batched delta already in a bucket becomes undecodable with no gate failing, because the golden and the code moved together. Fix is two edits in the notes paragraph: state the ASSERTION property (per-segment triple asserted after round-trip AND after commitAll, naming the partial hoist as the mutation), and say the discriminating golden is a NEW file, not an edit to chain-delta-batched-v1.bin.

findings.summary: The Java-site sweep is substantially applied but its count and its provenance claim are both wrong, MEASURED against the staged tree. `git grep -n 'podId, flushSeq' -- '*.java'` returns ELEVEN lines, not ten: Checkpoint.java:32, IngestCommitPathTest.java:81, CommitRequest.java:19, Sequencer.java:35, Sequencer.java:46, Sequencer.java:88, CommitProtocolSimulation.java:58, CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest.java:23, FakeSequencerTest.java:178, FakeSequencer.java:27 AND FakeSequencer.java:29. The notes name eleven line references but head the list 'TEN JAVA SITES', and the two sets are not the same eleven: FakeSequencer.java:29 ('Until then a replayed {@code (podId, flushSeq)} is treated as a NEW commit and assigned fresh offsets, here and in the real implementation alike') is a grep hit that is NOT named, while `Sequencer.java:51` IS named and is not a grep hit -- the quoted sentence ('carried from this first commit precisely so M4.10 can make the retry safe without changing the record shape') spans Sequencer.java:48-50, and line 51 is ` * {@link binjava.sequencer.FakeSequencer} does not model it either.` So the sentence 'git grep -n ... finds them' is false for one named site and silently omits one found site.
findings.failure_scenario: An M4.10c session reconciles the grep's eleven hits against a list headed 'ten', concludes the extra hit is already covered, and leaves FakeSequencer.java:29 standing. After M4.10d that sentence is false in the direction that matters -- a same-incarnation replay is no longer 'treated as a NEW commit ... in the real implementation alike' -- in the one file whose own javadoc says a fake that quietly differs from the real implementation is worse than no fake at all. Low impact only because :27 and :29 sit in one javadoc paragraph.

findings.summary: The pre-change-checkpoint consequence states the CHOICE without the COST of the choice. It says the recovered window 'is empty for those pods', that decode must accept an enumerated {0,1}, and that 'The empty window is ACCEPTED rather than refused: refusing would suppress legitimate commits, which is this ADR's stated primary harm. It closes at the first post-upgrade checkpoint.' It never says what accepting produces: during that window a genuine replay of a pre-upgrade commit matches nothing, is treated as new, and is assigned a SECOND set of offsets for records that already hold one. That is the duplication FR-3 and this whole row exist to prevent, in the opposite direction, and M4.10b's own task text calls out this exact direction ('against a pre-upgrade checkpoint nothing matches, so a real replay is ACCEPTED TWICE rather than a real commit suppressed').
findings.failure_scenario: A rolling upgrade with a mixed-version fleet: an old-build ingester's commit lands ambiguously, the response is lost, the retry arrives at a new-build sequencer that recovered from the pre-change checkpoint, and the same records are assigned a second offset range. An operator reading ADR-0036 during that upgrade finds no statement that duplication is possible in the window, so the incident is diagnosed against the wrong invariant. One sentence naming the accepted cost, and bounding it to the first post-upgrade checkpoint, closes it.
